audit.why: The chart already reads Swain / Swain / Skill / Skill / Sejuani / Skill / Skill in both layers, matching the mirror audit exactly and matching the 54.62% win rate over 119 games. No flips proposed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike calls Glacial Prison 'long-range' with no number, and no cooldown appears for it or for Demonic Ascension.
audit.why: Glacial Prison is 1300 range on 120/105/90; Nevermove is 850 and Demonic Ascension 120s. The gap of 450 units is the entire reason you cannot stand in the open at 6, and the R-for-R trade only makes sense with both cooldowns stated.
audit.corrected: 1300 vs 850 in the level-6 spike; 120s written into mid so the R-for-R trade is countable.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields say Frost stacks come from her autos ('Permafrost CC stacks off her autos', 'her Permafrost passive lets her build CC stacks passively off autos', wants.foe[1] 'Stack Permafrost passive by auto-attacking you').
audit.why: Riot's text puts Frost stacks on Winter's Wrath — 'Sejuani swings her mace twice, dealing damage, slowing enemies and applying Frost stacks' — and Permafrost is the separate E that 'freezes and stuns an enemy champion that has maximum Frost stacks', on a 1.5s cooldown at 560. So the thing to dodge is the W mace swing, not the autos. A player told to avoid autos will stand in exactly the wrong place.
audit.corrected: Winter's Wrath applies the Frost stacks; Permafrost is the stun that follows within 1.5s once they are maxed. Fury of the North then shatters the stunned target for a large magic hit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Glacial Prison is called an 'AoE stun' in whys[6], spikes[1] and late; early calls Sejuani a tank 'with no poke and no early disengage' and says she 'cannot burst you back or kite out'; wants.you[1] calls her body 'slow immobile'.
audit.why: Glacial Prison stuns only the first champion hit — the ice storm slows everyone else. Arctic Assault is a 650 charge that knocks you into the air, down 18s at rank 1, so she is not immobile and does have an engage. And Fury of the North grants slow immunity while Frost Armor is up, so a W landed on an out-of-combat Sejuani does not actually hold her.
audit.corrected: Stun on first hit, slow on the rest; Arctic Assault is a 650 knock-up on 18s; Frost Armor makes her slow-immune until you break it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (P Frost Armor slow immunity, Q 650 cd 18/16.5/15/13.5/12, R text)

audit.why: The packet's suspectNames hit on "Glacial Prison's" in whys[6] is a false positive — it is the correct name in possessive form, flagged only by edit distance. Not 'fixed'.

edits.before: She is gaining tank stats and you are burning mana; Permafrost CC stacks off her autos and her durability absorbs Q bolts more comfortably, making the window feel even rather than clearly yours.
edits.after: She is gaining tank stats and you are burning mana; Winter's Wrath applies the Frost stacks that arm Permafrost, so once the double mace swing lands the stun follows on a 1.5s cooldown and the window is hers.

edits.before: Stack Permafrost passive by auto-attacking you into your own R sustain window so her passive CC enables the R long-distance stun
edits.after: Land Winter's Wrath twice to max your Frost stacks so Permafrost stuns you, then shatter you with Fury of the North's bonus damage

edits.before: Your max-HP Soul Fragment stack and R sustain outlast her attrition in a 1v1, but Glacial Prison's teamfight AoE stun means the outcome stays skill-dependent — avoid grouping carelessly where her R hits your whole team.
edits.after: Your max-HP Soul Fragment stack and R sustain outlast her attrition in a 1v1, but Glacial Prison stuns whoever it hits first and only slows the rest, so it still decides fights — never be the body its bola finds first.

edits.before: Sejuani's R (Glacial Prison) is a long-range AoE stun she can fire before you can react — respect the range at 6 and keep the E root as your bail-out, not your opener.
edits.after: Glacial Prison flies 1300 and stuns the first champion it hits — 450 further than your Nevermove reaches, so break line of sight at 6 and keep the root as your bail-out, not your opener.

edits.before: Zone her off CS with W placed directly on top of her slow immobile body — she cannot reliably dodge the delayed orb
edits.after: Zone her off CS with W on her body, but her out-of-combat Frost Armor is slow-immune, so the orb chips her and does not hold her

edits.before: At levels 1-2, Sejuani has almost no trading pattern — her kit is a melee engage tank with no poke and no early disengage. Drop W directly on her feet every time she steps up to last-hit; the delayed orb hits a stationary target reliably, and even a modest slow makes it nearly undodgeable on her body. The moment E comes online at level 2, look for the straight E root-into-pull combo: root her, yank the fragment, and follow with Q bolts into her body. She cannot burst you back or kite out. Keep your mana healthy — you burn through it fast at this stage — and accept that you will not all-in her alone at levels 1-3, but you will win the fragment and poke war decisively.
edits.after: At levels 1-2 Sejuani has almost no trading pattern — no poke at all, and her only step-up is Arctic Assault, a 650 charge that knocks you into the air and is down 18s at rank 1. Drop W on her feet every time she walks up to last-hit, but know that Frost Armor makes her immune to slows until you have already broken it, so the orb chips rather than holds. The moment E comes online at level 2, look for the root-into-pull: Nevermove roots on its RETURN pass, so aim it past her, then yank the fragment and follow with Q bolts. Keep your mana healthy — you burn it fast here — and accept you will not all-in her alone at levels 1-3, but you will win the fragment and poke war decisively.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a grinding phase where you accumulate fragments through repeated W-into-E poke cycles, but Sejuani's growing tank stats start absorbing your Q burst more comfortably. Be careful not to overcommit: she may have Iceborn Gauntlet or early Frostfire backing her durability, and her Permafrost passive lets her build CC stacks passively off autos so any extended trade you let her have goes her way. At level 6 the equation shifts briefly in her favor — Glacial Prison is a long-range projectile that stuns you before you can R, so you cannot play aggressive in the open against a competent Sejuani without watching for that global threat. Save your own R for when she burns hers; your Demonic Ascension sustain answers her sustained auto-attack pattern cleanly once her R is spent.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a grinding phase where you accumulate fragments through repeated W-into-E poke cycles, but Sejuani's growing tank stats start absorbing your Q burst more comfortably. Be careful not to overcommit: Frost stacks come from Winter's Wrath, not from her autos, so the moment both mace swings land Permafrost is a 1.5s-cooldown stun waiting on you, and Fury of the North shatters a stunned target for a large magic hit. At level 6 the equation shifts briefly in her favour — Glacial Prison is a 1300-range projectile that stuns you from outside your 850 Nevermove, so do not stand in the open. Save your R for when she burns hers; it is 120s at rank 1, and your drain answers her once it is spent.

notes: No chart edits: both layers already agree with each other, with the mirror, and with the 54.62% win rate. The recurring 'Permafrost stacks off her autos' error appears in three fields and all three are corrected here. Frost Armor's slow immunity is worth a second look in itemization — Rylai's Crystal Scepter is listed as a core follow-up in report[8] and its slow is blanked while Frost Armor is up, though it still applies once she is in combat, so I did not propose an item change.
